title: New bank details before close
scenario: A long-standing supplier emails at 4:42 p.m. saying today’s €84,000 invoice must be paid to a new account because its bank is “under maintenance.” The thread contains real prior correspondence and the quarter closes today.

answers.A: Pause the payment and verify the bank change through a known supplier contact and your normal change-control process.
answers.B: Ask the supplier to confirm the change through your procurement portal or another established channel.
answers.C: Send a small test payment so the main invoice can still be released before close.

explanation: Compromised threads make payment-diversion fraud look routine. A test transfer proves only that the destination can receive money.
proTip: New bank details are a verification event, not an accounting update.
